Friend built a niche news site with Lovable using WordPress as headless CMS; Lovable built a monstrosity with Cloudflare workers, no proper caching, 3+ second TTFB. Switched to Cursor/Astro and it became blazing fast.

Signed up for Lovable, picked a template, got a disclaimer to 'take responsibility over project security, compliance, data, operations' with copy/paste disabled. 'I rest my case, your honor... It makes Squarespace look like a good product!'
"Fwiw loveable is fun and enables playful little apps. I enjoy it"
"It is crazy that people still use Lovable when we have codex and claude code...."
"I'm using Lovable heavily for PM prototyping and it's great. I think, if anything, current subscription may be too cheap!"
"Perhaps me just stupid and do prompts bad, but I can't make Lovable come up with anything really differentiated as a design."

"I don't get how this company makes money. Everyone who uses these tools is just building prototypes. They get to 60-70% functionality, but when it comes to actually productionize and launch, 99% of these projects will get abandoned."

"Lovable is a nice Website or App builder. Nothing for professionals, unless they want to build an prototype. Even building MVPs is nearly impossible... Lovable is promising a bit to much for my taste."
Startup CTO uses Lovable heavily for internal dashboards/CRUD tools; saved the equivalent of two full-time developers, but generated code is only okay, lacks sane defaults, abuses the 'any' type.

"I recently used lovable to create the scaffolding for an app. It did a great job, far better than I expected. However, it also squishes everything into one JS file, making it unwieldy for anything moderately complex... integrating onnx was basically impossible."
"A huge issue with lovable... is the app backend. Lovable took a shortcut and partnered with supabase but that deal will not last... There will be a reckoning."
"The churn from companies like lovable is indeed very high, and user frustration is high also."

"As a product designer, I'm seriously looking at using Lovable for quick ideation and prototyping. Showing users a series of Figma screens can be nice, but virtually everybody responds better to an interactive prototype."

"Lovable is marketed to non developers, so their core users wouldn't understand a security flow if it flashed red... Several were made on lovable. Now they are mostly abandoned, waiting for the subscription to expire... and their personal data to get exposed I guess."
